newsitem.title: USA: IBP sees market-ready cattle improving.
newsitem.headline: IBP sees market-ready cattle improving.

text.p: IBP Inc, which earlier reported lower third-quarter earnings, said Thursday it expects the availability of market-ready cattle to begin improving late this year or early next year.
A temporary decline in available cattle supplies in the third quarter put pressure on operating margins, IBP said.
"However, placements into feedlots this summer indicate that the availability of market ready cattle will begin to improve in late 1996 or early 1997," said Chairman Robert Peterson.
Earlier, IBP reported its third-quarter earnings fell to $40.5 million, or $0.42 a share, from $85.4 million, or $0.88, in the same period last year.
The results show IBP's protein complex was successful despite difficult industry conditions, IBP said.

International sales were flat during the first nine months of the year, the company said. The outbreak of a bacterial illness in Japan spurred a food-safety panic among consumers, which significantly reduced IBP's exports to the Pacific Rim during the third quarter, even though the source of the illnesses remains unknown, it said.
